key_features.feature1_subtitle: Armbian is a highly optimized OS specialized for single board computers.
key_features.feature2_subtitle: Home Assistant, Pi-Hole, Portainer, Cockpit, Plex Media Server, Docker, ...
key_features.feature3_subtitle: You can recreate provided images or build one with your changes.

uefi_devices.title: Generic / UEFI
uefi_devices.note: Suitable for hardware that supports UEFI boot mode.

getting_started.step1_content: Find your board and download one of the available images. Archives can be written with Etcher or USBimager (all OS).
getting_started.step2_content: Make sure you have a good and reliable SD card and a proper power supply. Insert the SD card into a slot and power the board. First boot takes up to 30 seconds with an average SD card and on the cheapest board.
getting_started.step3_content: First root login on HDMI or serial console is automatic. If you connect via SSH, login as root (password: 1234). You will be prompted to change the password. Next, you will be asked to create a normal user account that is sudo enabled (beware of QWERTY keyboard settings at this stage).
getting_started.step4_content: Type 'sudo armbian-config' and change timezone, reconfigure language, locales, network. Manage OpenSSHD settings, freeze kernel upgrades, toggle hardware settings. Install Armbian to internal or external memory.
